sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Bradley County, Tennessee?
sections.html:
Two county offices split the work. The Assessor of Property sets appraisals and hears appeals, and the Trustee bills and collects. The Trustee's FAQ says plainly that the Trustee has no authority over the amount of an assessment.

  • Assessor of Property: Stanley Thompson, Courthouse Annex, 155 Broad Street NW, Room 105, Cleveland. Phone 423-728-7125.
  • Trustee: Tim Akins, 1701 Keith Street NW, Cleveland, TN 37311. Phone 423-728-7247. Hours are Monday through Thursday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Pay by phone at 833-591-7276.
  • City of Cleveland taxes: Cleveland City Clerk, 190 Church Street NE. Phone 423-472-4551.
  • Delinquent tax sales: the Chancery Court Clerk and Master, 423-728-7209.

A house inside Cleveland gets two bills, one from the county and one from the city. The city's tax page says so directly. A house in Bradley County outside any city gets the county bill only.

sections.h2: How is a Bradley County property tax bill calculated?
sections.html:
Tennessee multiplies the appraised value by an assessment ratio, then applies the tax rate per $100 of assessed value. The Comptroller lists the ratio at 25 percent for residential and farm property and 40 percent for commercial and industrial property.

Bradley County's 2026 net property tax rate is $1.0772 per $100 of assessed value. County-only properties in the fire service district pay an extra $0.2558, for a combined $1.3330. Charleston adds a city rate of $0.3655, which brings the combined county and city figure to $1.4427. For Cleveland's rate, the trustee's page tells owners to call the city at 423-472-4551.

Here is an example using the Census Bureau's median owner-occupied home value for Bradley County of $261,900. At 25 percent, the assessed value is $65,475. At $1.0772 per $100, the county tax is about $705. At the combined fire-district rate of $1.3330, it is about $873. Your own bill will differ, because it rests on the assessor's appraisal of your parcel and not on a county median.

sections.h2: When are Bradley County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills go out in October to the owner of record as of January 1, and the county says they must be paid by the last day of February. The trustee's page lists February 27, 2027 as the due date for the 2026 taxes and gave October 1, 2026 as the estimated mailing date for notices.

Starting March 1, interest of 1.5 percent per month (18 percent a year) is added on the first of each month. Mailed payments count by postmark date, and the night deposit box counts as that day. Partial payments on current taxes are accepted by mail or in the office, while online payments must be in full.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Bradley County assessment?
sections.html:
Appeals start with the Local Board of Equalization, and the assessor's office books the appointments. The assessor's page says owners with a changed appraisal receive a notice by mail beginning May 20, 2027, that the board begins meeting June 1, 2027, and that the last day to schedule an appointment for the 2027 session is June 17, 2027.

An owner must appear personally, or send an agent who carries the owner's written authorization. The page warns that failing to appear and appeal makes the assessment final without further right of appeal. It cites T.C.A. 67-5-508. A letter of authorization form and an informal review request form are posted on the assessor's site, and the office can be reached at 423-728-7125 or assessor@bradleycountytn.gov.

If the county board does not settle it, the next step is the State Board of Equalization. The Comptroller says that appeal is due by August 1 of the tax year or within 45 days of the date the county board's notice was sent, whichever is later.

sections.h2: What tax relief is available to Bradley County homeowners?
sections.html:
Tennessee reimburses part or all of the local taxes paid on a primary residence for low-income elderly and disabled homeowners and for disabled veterans. The Comptroller stresses that relief is a state payment, not an exemption, so the owner still receives a bill and must pay it.

  • Age: an elderly applicant turns 65 on or before December 31 of the tax year.
  • Income: Bradley County's FAQ lists a combined limit of $38,470 based on 2025 income, counting all living owners of record plus the applicant's spouse.
  • Disabled veterans: relief applies to the first $175,000 of market value of the home.
  • Ownership: you must document ownership during the tax year, for example with a tax bill, warranty deed or probated will.
  • Timing: new applicants for tax relief and tax freeze sign up from October 1, 2026 through April 5, 2027.

Only the primary residence qualifies in a given year, and the state does not forward relief checks. Applications are available from the Trustee's office, and the relief coordinator is reachable at 423-728-7247.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when you sell a Bradley County house?
sections.html:
Taxes stay with the property. The county's FAQ says that if the deed changes after January 1, the bill still goes to the owner of record as of that date, and the new owner can ask for a copy. Unpaid taxes keep accruing against the parcel.

The closing statement should show how the year's tax was split. Bradley County tells new owners to check with the title company or review the closing statement to see how it was settled. Sellers who have not paid the prior year should clear it at or before closing, because interest runs 1.5 percent a month from March 1.

If taxes go unpaid long enough, the Clerk and Master can sell the parcel at auction. The county FAQ says the buyer cannot take possession until one year after the sale is confirmed, the redemption interest is 10 percent a year, and all liens except state and federal liens are cleared. Cleveland's page adds that city delinquent taxes go to the Clerk and Master after 12 months of penalty.

Bradley County had an estimated 115,465 residents in July 2025, with 67.3 percent of homes owner-occupied and a median household income of $66,552. The county does not mail its bill to your mortgage company, so if a lender escrows your taxes, forward the bill. A seller who pays directly should keep the receipt for the closing agent.

faqs.q: What is the Bradley County property tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The county net rate is $1.0772 per $100 of assessed value. With the fire service district it is $1.3330, and in Charleston the combined county and city rate is $1.4427. Cleveland sets its own rate, available from the city at 423-472-4551.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Bradley County property taxes?
faqs.a: Pay the Trustee at 1701 Keith Street NW, Cleveland, by phone at 833-591-7276, or online. Cleveland city taxes go to the City Clerk at 190 Church Street NE.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to pay 2026 Bradley County taxes?
faqs.a: The trustee lists February 27, 2027. After that, interest of 1.5 percent is added on the first of each month starting March 1.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Bradley County taxes in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, by mail or in the office, as long as current-year taxes are paid in full by the February due date. Online payments must be the full amount due. The trustee's page lists a partial payment signup from October 1, 2026 through February 5, 2027.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Bradley County property value?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor of Property at 423-728-7125. Appeals go first to the Local Board of Equalization, which the assessor's office schedules. The Trustee cannot change an assessment.
